query: What pragmatic approximations or prioritization heuristics reduce compute for 3D hierarchical occlusion and ensemble fusion while preserving explanation fidelity?

response.query: What pragmatic approximations or prioritization heuristics reduce compute for 3D hierarchical occlusion and ensemble fusion while preserving explanation fidelity?
response.answer: Multi-resolution 3D approximations and hierarchical Z-buffer occlusion culling reduce compute for 3D rendering. Ensemble fusion with occlusion handling uses orthogonal fusion to maintain accuracy. These techniques optimize computational load while preserving fidelity.

results.title: Prioritization Heuristics - Humanizing Work
results.content:
Title: Prioritization Heuristics - Humanizing Work
First, it allows the person prioritizing to better understand, reason about, and tune their intuition. The heuristics are also really helpful for personal prioritization-the same rules apply to figuring out what to focus on today and what to say no to. **Guarantee one** – If I could guarantee one of these got accomplished (somehow) [today, this week, etc.], which one would I use my guarantee on? **Choose the bottom** (to eliminate) – If one of these was for sure not going fit, which one would I feel best about letting go of? **Pairwise** (20/20 vision) – “Number 1 or number 2. **Hierarchical prioritization** – Prioritize your projects, do your next actions for each project in the priority order of the projects. **Simple ROI** – What’s the return on each item? **Cost of Delay** – How does the ROI change over time? **2-Minute Rule** – Will it be faster to just do it than to capture the task on my todo list? **Urgent vs Important** – It’s easy to confuse these. **Covey Rocks vs Sand** – You have to move some river rocks and some sand. **Prohibit LIFO** – What would I do next if the most recent additions to my list weren’t an option? **Sustainability** – What items will most serve longer-term sustainability for me, my team, larger systems I’m a part of? **Optionality** – When facing complexity…What can I do today that will give me more options in the future when I’ll know more? **Maximize leverage** – What item will have disproportionate results? **Key Stakeholders** – Sometimes, an item is important not because it’s important to you but because it’s important to someone else—and that relationship is important to you. **Exploit the Constraint** – When your tasks are part of something larger and the overall result is limited by your capacity…What’s the thing you’re uniquely able to do? **Batching** – Some small things aren’t worth the task switching overhead, but can have positive results when batched so you can focus on several in succession. **Energy as data** – The things you’re particularly drawn to might be important and purposeful. **Resistance as data** – Your internal resistance is also a source of info.

results.title: (PDF) Multi-resolution 3D approximations for rendering complex scenes
results.content: A 3-Dimensional (3-D) object modeling technique with mesh simplification and refinement based resolution adjustment is proposed in this paper. In this paper we present a new technique for view-dependent LOD rendering, where the scene is represented through an octree model from which we can obtain a triangle mesh corresponding to a view-dependent LOD. In this paper we present a new technique for view-dependent LOD rendering, where the scene is represented through an octree model from which we can obtain a triangle mesh corresponding to a view-dependent LOD. The paper demonstrates that multi-resolution 3D approximations significantly reduce computational load while maintaining visual fidelity, achieving up to 40% lower rendering times compared to uniform resolution models. This paper presents a new approach to rendering arbitrary views of real-world 3-D objects of complex shapes. Adaptive real-time level-of-detail based rendering for polygonal models. We present an algorithm for performing adaptive real-time level-of-detail-based rendering for triangulated polygonal models. The most robust and rapid approach to keeping the overall number of polygons low is to use mesh simplification algorithms to create low-poly versions of preexisting, high-poly models. This paper presents a new approach for generating coarse-level approximations of topologically complex models. Many such algorithms are based on mesh decimation techniques, generating coarse triangulations while optimizing for a particular metric which models the distance to the original shape. Motivated by the current requirements of digital 3D museums in the low bandwidth networks, we present a novel and efficient approximation algorithm based on axial symmetry of 3D pottery model. In this paper, we reduce data for mesh representation while preserving the geometric approximation as well as the model quality of the resulting mesh. Compared with available mesh simplification algorithms and using the same amount of data to represent the model, the proposed approach gives significant improvement in the accuracy of the approximated 3D potteries. A digital elevation model and digital ortho-photo map data integrated algorithm is proposed as the base algorithm for our approach to build a realistic 3D terrain scene. We propose a technique for performing view-dependent simpli cations for level-of-detail-based renderings of complex models.

results.title: Hierarchical Z-Buffer Occlusion Culling - Nick Darnell’s Blog
results.content:
Title: Hierarchical Z-Buffer Occlusion Culling - Nick Darnell’s Blog
# Hierarchical Z-Buffer Occlusion Culling. ### Hierarchical Z-Buffer Culling Steps. 3. GPU – Render the remaining occluders to a ‘depth buffer’. The ‘depth buffer’ should just be mip 0 in a full mip chain of render targets (not the actual depth buffer). You’ll do this by rendering a fullscreen effect with a pixel shader taking the last level of the mip chain and down sampling it into the next, preserving the highest depth value in a sample group of 4 pixels. For DX11, you can just constrain the shader resource view so that you can both read and render from the same mip chain. For DX9 you’ll have to use StretchRect to copy from a second mip chain, since you can’t sample and render to the same mip chain in DX9. 6. GPU – DX11 send the list of bounds to a compute shader, which computes the screen space width of the sphere then uses the width to compute the mip level to sample from the HiZ map generated in step 4, such that the sphere covers no more than 2 pixels wide. Instead of a compute shader you’ll process the vertices using a vertex shader, you’ll also need to use the pixel location provided in the texcoord stream to make sure the results of the test are written out to that point in a render target, and in a pixel shader you’ll need to do the sampling to test to see if it’s visible, and output a color like white for culled, black for visible. 7. CPU – Try to do some work on the CPU after the occluder rendering and culling process is kicked off, for me the entire process took about 0.74 ms of GPU time on a Radeon 5450, with 900 bounds. For DX9 you’ll have to copy the render target rendered to in step 6 containing the checker pattern of black and white pixels and then iterate over the pixels on the CPU to know what is visible and what is hidden. ### Hierarchical Z-Buffer Culling Code. Here’s my sample implementation of the Hierarchical Z-Buffer Culling solution in DX11 and DX9.

results.title: Robust ensemble person reidentification via orthogonal fusion with occlusion handling - ScienceDirect
results.content:
Title: Robust ensemble person reidentification via orthogonal fusion with occlusion handling - ScienceDirect
# Robust ensemble person reidentification via orthogonal fusion with occlusion handling. To achieve robust Re-ID without manually labeling occluded regions, we propose to take an ensemble learning-based approach derived from the analogy between arbitrarily shaped occluded regions and robust feature representation. Using the orthogonality principle, our developed deep CNN model uses masked autoencoder (MAE) and global–local feature fusion for robust person identification. Second, some work, such as the semantic-aware occlusion-robust network (SORN) [11] and high-order Re-ID [12] addresses the issue of occlusion at the higher semantic level, i.e., both local and global information contained in the occluded images will be extracted and combined adaptively to improve the robustness of the overall system. Recognizing the analogy between image retrieval (the target application of DOLG) and person Re-ID, an ID-preserving person ReID model can be developed utilizing effective local–global feature fusion for occlusion handling. To design a ReID model invariant to occlusion, we propose an orthogonal fusion with occlusion handling (OFOH) model based on Transformer architecture that generates an occlusion-invariant feature space. We propose an approach that uses an ensemble learning paradigm for the occluded person Re-ID problem. We apply orthogonal fusion to our CNN model that helps learn discriminative global and body-part local features that avoid interference with occlusion. Among the most influential works on person Re-ID, the harmonious attention network [18] has shown the advantages of jointly learning attention selection and feature representation in a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) by maximizing complementary information at different levels of visual attention subject to discriminative learning constraints of Re-ID. In this paper, we propose a deep ensemble learning framework for occlusion handling for person reidentification. Our approach learns a robust latent representation for the occluded person Re-ID problem using two deep models. This paper presents an ensemble learning-based approach to occluded person Re-ID that uses both CNN and Transformer architecture. ### Semantic-aware occlusion-robust network for occluded person reidentification. ### Body part-based representation learning for occluded person reidentification. Occluded person re-identification (Re-ID), which aims to retrieve images of the same individual under partial occlusion, remains a significant challenge in real-world surveillance scenarios and has attracted growing attention in recent years. * ### Token recombination based shallow-deep feature fusion for occluded person re-identification.
